blocks.h2: Replacing a Heater in a 1950s Basement
blocks.body: Skokie basements from the 1950s often have narrow stairs, low ceilings and a chimney shared with the furnace. Before quoting, we check the path in, the space and the venting. If the furnace has been replaced with a high-efficiency model that vents out the side, the water heater may need a chimney liner. We'll tell you up front, so there are no surprises on install day.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Installation Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Will a new water heater fit down my basement stairs?
items.answer: Almost always. We measure the stairs and the space before we quote, and we'll tell you if a different size makes more sense.

items.q: Do I need a chimney liner for a new water heater?
items.answer: Sometimes. If the water heater is now the only appliance using the chimney, the flue may be too large. We test it and explain the options.
A standard swap usually takes a few hours.

items.q: Do you take the old tank?
items.answer: Yes. We drain it, disconnect it and haul it away.

items.q: Can I go from a 40 to a 50 gallon tank?
items.answer: Usually, if the space and gas line allow it.

items.q: How much does water heater replacement cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on size, type and venting. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the size, fuel type, venting and any code updates. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
